# About this book

Hello and welcome to the EcoMods working group!

In this document, you will (hopefully) find everything you need for your
course / internship / thesis with us.

The book is meant to be a live document, and will be updated continuously.
As you browse through sections, you will encounter empty or incomplete sections.
You're welcome to ask for sections to be added, updated, or even better, improve
it yourself! See section \@ref(contributing).

## Acknowldegements and licensing

This manual is an update of a manual of the [original Ecomods](CCTB-Ecomods/Ecomods-Booklet) at the University
of Würzburg. Huge thanks to them for assembling this knowledge base!

The manual is published under the terms of the [MIT License](https://github.com/biob-ecomod/ecomods_booklet/blob/main/LICENSE), which means you can
freely copy, modify and share its contents as long as you acknowledge the original
work and provide a copyright notice and copy in the license in all derived works.

## Contributing to this book

We gladly accept any suggestions on how to improve this guide, so
let us know if you feel that anything is missing!

This booklet is a bookdown document. This means, that it
consists of several R Markdown files. To learn R markdown see section
\@ref(rmd). The booklet is hosted on
[GitHub](https://github.com/CCTB-Ecomods/Ecomods-Booklet) (see section
\@ref(version-control).

1.  Step: Clone the repository from GitHub.

2.  Step: Open the .rmd file of the Chapter you would like to change.

3.  Step: Do your changes.

4.  Step: Commit your changes and push them on GitHub.

5.  Step: Then the magic happens: via github actions the website will be
    updated, but this takes 5-10 Minutes (check the green dot!). This
    creates files that are pushed automatically. Therefore, don't work
    within the Repo while waiting and **pull the changes** before you go
    on editing.

Don't forget to add links, citations, figures etc in a nice and
organized way. Check text for typos and readability and be sure that a
beginner can understand it.

## Missing sections and TODOs within this booklet

If you find any missing topics, collect them here or write a *TODO* at
the appropriate part.

## People



## Induction

Welcome to the group! We hope you have a great time with us and that your 
experience in your lab will be the opportunity to develop your academic skills
and explore exciting research!

Here are the things you should be upon starting your projects:

-   **Keys**: our lab is hosted in the old NEES institute, Venusbergweg 22, at 
the edge of the Botanische Gärten. Access to the building and other facilities
of the institute is managed through transponders, which you must obtain in 
person from Elke Friesecke at the main Plant Biodiversity building. 
Upon leaving

- **Slack**: we have a Slack workspace for the group, which is our main channel
for communication. You will find links to the lab meeting schedule and zoom call
pinned in the #general channel. Ask another team member for an invite link!

- **Meetings**: save these time slots for obligatory participation:

    -   weekly CCTB seminar, Wednesdays 11:00-12:00
    -   weekly EcoMods lab meeting, Thursdays 13:30-15:00

- **IT questions:** Theo can help with all research-related software enquiries.
For hardware issues, you can contact Tomi Balen.

We hope that this document helps you to learn more about how to do
Ecological Modeling group and how to navigate life at BIOB. If you have
any questions, you can come by our offices or send us an email any time.

-   **University Library:** before using the services of the ULB (Universitäts
un Landesbibliothek Bonn), you will need to get yourself a library ID card (Bibliothekausweis) and a user account, which are not automatically created upon
joining the University. The procedure is detailed on the [ULB website](https://www.ulb.uni-bonn.de/de/nutzung-und-ausleihe/ausweis-konto).
